title: Tuba, solos at church, then violin
summary: In Oakland he borrowed a tuba through the school system, played "Silent Night" at nine or ten, then took up violin from a church lady's gift.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: And what instrument did you start on?

I really started on tuba. Possibly an explanation of why I started on the various instruments is because in Oakland, California, they had a very good school system, and if your parent would sign a bond, you could take out any instrument that you wanted to learn. And so I took out tuba, and I stayed with that for a while until I became fairly well acquainted with the three-valved instruments, and -- in fact, I got so good on the three-valves, that I could play a solo. And one of my first solos was 'Silent Night,' which I played at the Christmas festival in our church.
That was when you were about what age?
Oh, I was about nine or ten years old then, uh-huh.
And how long did you play that instrument?

Well, it got too heavy for me, and for a while I didn't know which instrument to pick up then. And I finally acquired a taste for violin, and I liked it so well that I used to try to make violins out of cigar boxes with boards and everything. And I had some very good friends in the church, and one old lady decided to give me a violin for Christmas, much to my chagrin. As it turned out, I took it for a few months, oh, quite a little time. In fact, I would say almost two years or more, during which -- [PAUSE]
